Subject: DPA: request for subprocessor evidence + runtime telemetry opt-out

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed the DPA. Procurement has two open items before we can sign: one operational, one contractual. High level: we need (1) evidence for the listed subprocessors (SOC2 / attestations) and (2) a mechanism in contract to ensure our runtime traffic and prefix telemetry is not exported to downstream analytics by Redwood for customers who opt-out.

Specifically:
- Can you provide SOC2 summary/audit attestations for the subprocessors on your list, and a short CSV mapping each vendor to control areas?
- Our legal wants a clause that guarantees no analytics export for our runtime requests (we call this a telemetry opt-out). They asked whether you can support a per-account runtime flag or some contractual exhibit to enforce this.

Procurement also asked for a proposed redline so they can move quickly. We're trying to keep training/data-use language narrow (no model training or downstream analytics for our runtime data).

We can jump on a quick sync if helpful — our legal is on the thread (contracts@novamed.com). DocuSign queue is waiting once we confirm these pieces.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — target for signing is end of month.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connell

Kimberly / Olga,

We can provide the following: a SOC 2 Type II summary (high level controls), and a CSV with the subprocessor list mapped to the control areas they cover and contract links. We typically share the SOC2 summary + subprocessor CSV over a secure link; full reports require an access request. That's standard. I'll put the links in the draft response.

On the telemetry opt-out: security view is that we can support an "export opt-out" at multiple levels: contractual (a clause that prohibits telemetry export for a given customer) and runtime (a per-customer flag that disables telemetry export paths). Two notes:
- The runtime flag will need to short-circuit the export pipeline; because telemetry paths are used for health/ops metrics and model quality tooling, disabling them for an account will reduce the observability signal for Redwood and may impact automated model-quality alerts; we should be explicit about that trade-off in the redline.
- We need to confirm what NovaMed classifies as "telemetry" vs "runtime payload". If they consider certain metadata (full prompts, user identifiers) to be prohibited, call that out — some of that data touches operational routing.

Attachments I will provide to Kimberly for customer share:
- subprocessor_list.csv (stub with vendor, country, controls covered)
- soc2_summary.pdf (one-page summary)

I recommend we: (A) draft contractual language that forbids analytics export of runtime payloads and (B) offer a configuration plan (feature flag) we can implement and roll out to the account before signing if feasible.

Marcus

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA: request for subprocessor evidence + runtime telemetry opt-out

Thanks — quick product note and suggested approach.

Product feasibility:
- We already have an internal feature toggle framework and per-tenant config. Implementing a runtime-level telemetry opt-out is possible but not trivial: the telemetry export pipeline is interleaved with prefix/KV cache metrics and automated batching heuristics.
- Two implementation options:
  1) Contractual-only + conservative runtime change: add a server-side flag that prevents telemetry export for the tenant. This is the fastest path (~2-3 weeks engineering work: feature flag + gating in export pipeline + Console toggle exposed to sales/CS). We can deliver a safe rollout with monitoring and a kill-switch. Performance impact: negligible for request latency but we will lose batch-level analytics; in certain high-throughput customers that can change batching behavior and increase cost marginally. We'll document that in the redline.
  2) Deep isolation: add per-tenant isolated export pipelines and stricter residency (longer, 6-10 weeks). This gives stronger guarantees but is heavier.

Recommended ask to Legal redline: a simple clause that says: "Customer may elect to opt-out of telemetry/analytics export for runtime requests; Redwood will implement a per-customer opt-out configuration and will not use opted-out runtime data for model training or downstream analytics." Add a pointer to a Schedule/Exhibit describing the technical implementation (feature-flag timeline and known limitations).

Proposed DPA wording (short):
"Telemetry Opt-Out. Upon Customer's written request, Redwood will disable telemetry export for Customer runtime requests for the duration set forth in the applicable Order Form. During the opt-out period Redwood will not use Customer runtime payloads for analytics or model training. Redwood will provide Customer with a technical description of the opt-out implementation and any operational trade-offs."

I'll attach a short design doc with the scope and rollout plan. If Legal insists on immediate contractual enforcement before implementation, we'll need to mark timelines and acceptance criteria (i.e., Redwood will not apply the telemetry prohibition until the feature is deployed and toggled for the Customer).

I'll also draft a short note we can send to NovaMed explaining the trade-offs.

Olga Petrov
VP, Product (Platform)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: featureflag_design.pdf (design + rollout plan), redline_proposal.docx (initial proposed wording)
